page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 256.0 GB of RAM, which yields a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the E32ds_v5 in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 31080.73 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13847.0. Memory read bandwidth reaches 1678.79 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 143.87 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, while write bandwidth is measured at 67.31 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation performance on small language models at 278.54 tokens/sec, though performance scales down to a weak 6.67 tokens/sec for prompt processing on large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ds_v5 offers high resource density by combining a substantial memory footprint with dedicated local storage on a single instance. This configuration reduces the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI training. The server is designed for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale web serving.
